title: Gauging the interplay between market liquidity and funding liquidity
summary: This ECB Financial Stability Review special feature examines how market liquidity and funding liquidity interact and can reinforce each other to generate liquidity spirals. It constructs composite indicators for both dimensions in the euro area and identifies structural and cyclical drivers. The authors note that market liquidity has become more fragile despite high excess reserves, driven by subdued free float of high-quality debt and elevated inflation uncertainty affecting monetary policy path expectations.
key_points: Market liquidity and funding liquidity are inherently connected and can amplify each other into liquidity spirals with systemic potential

Market liquidity has multiple dimensions: immediacy (pace of execution), breadth/depth (scope and size of transactions), tightness (cost and price impact), and resilience (ability of market-makers to continue during stress)

Funding liquidity risk manifests in three forms: rollover risk (inability to replace short-term funding), redemption risk (depositor withdrawals), and haircut/margining risk (collateral value changes)
Market liquidity is not directly observable and no single indicator captures all its dimensions; bond market data is sparse due to OTC trading prevalence and transparency rule waivers
High-frequency trading automation may undermine the robustness of individual liquidity measures
Cyclical determinants including investor risk appetite, macro conditions, and global monetary policy cycles have started turning restrictive as policy normalizes
why_it_matters: Understanding the interaction between market and funding liquidity is essential for assessing systemic financial stability risks. When market liquidity evaporates, asset pricing becomes unreliable and tends to overreact, increasing volatility and funding costs. This research provides a framework for monitoring liquidity conditions in the euro area and identifying when the two liquidity dimensions may reinforce each other dangerously.
market_structure_context: The paper addresses core market structure concepts: market-making practices, trade transparency, investor landscape, bid-ask spreads, OTC trading fragmentation, consolidated tape gaps, and high-frequency trading effects on liquidity. It also covers funding market structure including repo markets, margin mechanics, and the operational framework connecting intermediaries to market functioning.
